title: Garment workers clash with police during wage protests in Savar
seoTitle: Savar garment workers protest for higher wages

tea.why: Garment workers are protesting to demand a minimum monthly wage increase to Tk 30,000.
tea.want: A minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
tea.changed: Nov 5: Clashes between workers and police in Savar led to injuries and the deployment of Border Guard Bangladesh personnel.

summary: Garment workers in Savar and other industrial areas of Bangladesh have engaged in protests and road blockades to demand a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000. In Savar, demonstrations escalated into clashes with police near the Al-Muslim Group factory after authorities attempted to clear a blockade on the Dhaka-Aricha highway. According to Dhaka District Superintendent of Police Shamima Parveen, approximately 30,000 to 40,000 workers participated in the Savar area. The confrontation involved the use of bricks and stones by protesters and tear gas, sound grenades, and rubber bullets by police. A police vehicle was set on fire during the unrest. Over 200 factories in Savar and Ashulia have suspended operations. Three platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh have been deployed to maintain order in the industrial belt.
response: Police used tear gas, sound grenades, and rubber bullets to disperse protesters. Three platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh were deployed to the area to maintain security.

crowd.text: Between 30,000 and 40,000 workers had assembled in the area according to Dhaka District SP Shamima Parveen.

updates.text: Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway in Savar, leading to clashes with police and the deployment of Border Guard Bangladesh.

sources.title: Bangladesh: 50 injured, 200 factories shut as protests by garment workers turn violent
